rows.label: C1

rows.label: C2

blocks.title: What the construction explains: the surplus over the flavour data

rows.label: X1
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Koide ratio} is exactly $2/3$ given the quarter-turn realisation B5, the cube-root generation orbit bisected at the quarter-turn ($\rho^2=2^{-1}$), an exact value rather than an unexplained empirical coincidence.

rows.label: X2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The up-quark Koide value} is $5/6$ in framed arithmetic ($0.849$ in the working scheme, $0.832$ with pole masses), the cube-root colour norm $r_u^2=N(1-\omega)=3$ against the colourless $N(1-i)=2$, a ratio where the Standard Model carries no relation at all.

rows.label: X3
rows.predicate: \textbf{The flavour charges} are the role depths $(0,1,2)$ of the closed primitive-role ladder, derived as the three generative roles rather than assigned to fit the hierarchy.

rows.label: X4
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Cabibbo angle} is the Gatto relation $V_{us}=|\sqrt{m_d/m_s}-e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{m_u/m_c}|$ following from the role-depth texture, the leading term at $0.3\%$ and the phase $\varphi$ a kernel datum, so two otherwise-independent observables are tied rather than measured apart.

rows.label: X5
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Georgi--Jarlskog factor} is the colour count $N_c=3$, the $B\!-\!L$ Clebsch of the $\overline{\mathbf{126}}$, not a texture coefficient inserted by hand; its double ratio $9$ against the measured $10.4\pm0.5$ is the open $15\%$ excess of the minimal Clebsch.

rows.label: X6
rows.predicate: \textbf{The up-sector doubling} $m^u_i\sim(m^d_i)^2$ is forced by the $\mathbf{10}\cdot\mathbf{10}$ Yukawa, so the steeper up hierarchy is a consequence rather than a separate assumption.

rows.label: X7
rows.predicate: \textbf{The electron's extreme lightness} is the quarter-turn boundary: the lightest generation sits where the winding amplitude vanishes, massless at leading order, rather than an anomalously small Yukawa tuned by hand.

rows.label: X8
rows.predicate: \textbf{The large-lepton, small-quark mixing split} is the lopsided $M_e=M_d^{\mathsf T}$: one off-diagonal feeds the invisible right-handed quark rotation and, transposed, the visible left-handed lepton rotation, so the two mixing matrices are one structure rather than two unrelated ones.

rows.label: X9
rows.predicate: \textbf{The reactor angle} is, at leading order, $\sin\theta_{13}=\sin\theta_C/\sqrt2=0.159$, quark--lepton complementarity through the quarter-turn, $7\%$ above the observed $0.149$ with no correction derived: a leading-order estimate of the mixing parameter, not a prediction.

rows.label: X10
rows.predicate: \textbf{Near-maximal leptonic CP} is the cube-root phase: $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega=\sqrt3/2$ gives the maximal Jarlskog $J=1/(6\sqrt3)$, so the cubic reappears as CP violation rather than a free phase fitted to data.

rows.label: X11
rows.predicate: \textbf{The neutrino spectrum} (a near-massless lightest state, $\sum m_\nu\simeq59\,$meV on the normal branch) follows from colourlessness fixing $Q_\nu=2/3$, the transpose fixed point under the alignment $M_R\propto m_D$ (Y1) and the boundary branch that selects the ordering (B6), rather than three independent neutrino masses.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_eigen
C1.doc: 28:C1, 28:X11 — on a cube root `ω² + ω + 1 = 0` the circulant has the eigenvectors `(1, ω, ω²)` and `(1, ω², ω)` with the eigenvalues `λ₁ = a + bω + cω²` and `λ₂ = a + bω² + cω` (the first row gives `λ_k` itself; the second and third rows give `ω^k λ_k` and `ω^{2k} λ_k`); the eigenvector `(1, 1, 1)` has `λ₀ = a + b + c`. Universality makes the amplitude matrix a circulant, and this is its spectrum: the Koide functional form.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sum
C1.doc: 28:C1 — the eigenvalues sum to `3a`: `λ₀ + λ₁ + λ₂ = 3a`.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sumsq
C1.doc: 28:C1, 28:C2, 28:C11b — the squares of the eigenvalues sum to `3a² + 6bc`: at `c = b̄` this is `3a² + 6 N(b)`, so `Q = Σλ²/(Σλ)² = 1/3 + (2/3) N(b)/a²`, the Koide form with `ρ² = N(b)/a²` (`koide_parseval`).

C1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_parseval
C1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C1, 28:X1 — Parseval on the cube-root orbit `C₃`: for amplitudes `a₀, a₁, a₂` and `ω` with `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`, `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 â₁ â₂`, `â₀ = Σ a_j`, `â₁ = a₀ + a₁ω + a₂ω²`, `â₂ = a₀ + a₁ω² + a₂ω` — the Koide form `Q = Σ a_j² / (Σ a_j)² = 1/3 + (2/3)ρ²` with `ρ² = â₁â₂/â₀²`, exact on every shell carrying the root `ω`.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_extension
C2.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C2, 28:X1, 28:P1, on every shell: with `h + h = 1` and `ν = −3`, `ω = −h + h w` has `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`; `â₂ = â̄₁`, so `â₁ â₂ = N(â₁)`; Parseval `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 N(â₁)`; and `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 N(â₁) = â₀²` (`ρ² = 1/2`).

C2.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sumsq
C2.doc: 28:C1, 28:C2, 28:C11b — the squares of the eigenvalues sum to `3a² + 6bc`: at `c = b̄` this is `3a² + 6 N(b)`, so `Q = Σλ²/(Σλ)² = 1/3 + (2/3) N(b)/a²`, the Koide form with `ρ² = N(b)/a²` (`koide_parseval`).

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.quarter_turn_boundary
C3.doc: 28:C3, 28:X7 — the massless generation sits at the quarter-turn diagonal. With `i² = −1`, `ω² + ω + 1 = 0` and `h + h = 1`, the circulant `(a, b, c)` with `b = −h(1 + i) a ω²` and `c = −h(1 − i) a ω` (so `c = b̄` when `a, h` are real, `ī = −i`, `ω̄ = ω²`) has `λ₁ = a + bω + cω² = 0` and `2bc = a²`: the vanishing eigenvalue and the Koide value `Q = 2/3` (`2N(b) = a²`) at once.

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.lo_eigen
C3.doc: 28:C3, 28:X7 — the leading-order spectrum. At the boundary of `quarter_turn_boundary` the two remaining eigenvalues are `λ₀ = a h (3 + s)` and `λ₂ = a h (3 − s)` with `s = i (ω − ω²)`, and `s² = 3`: the square-root masses `(0, 3 − √3, 3 + √3)·ah`, the ratios `m_e : m_μ : m_τ = 0 : (2 − √3)² : 1`.

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.lo_ratio_sq
C3.doc: 28:C3, 28:X7 — with `s² = 3`, `(3 − s)² = (7 − 4s)(3 + s)²`: the leading-order ratio `(λ₂/λ₀)² = m_μ/m_τ` is `7 − 4√3 = (2 − √3)² ≈ 0.0718` (observed `0.0595`).

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.delta_lo
C3.doc: 28:C3 — the leading phase as a cycle fraction: `δ_LO = 3/8 − 1/3 = 1/24`, that is `9 − 8 = 1` over the common denominator `24 = 3 · 8`.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.norm_one_sub_i
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2, 00:G17 — the quarter-turn norm: `(1 − i)(1 + i) = 2` on every shell with `i² = −1`; the squared amplitude of a colourless sector, `r² = N(1 − i) = 2`, so `Q = 1/3 + r²/6 = 2/3`.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.norm_one_sub_omega
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2, 00:G17 — the colour norm: `N(1 − ω) = 3` for the cube root `ω = −h + h w` of the extension at `ν = −3` (`h + h = 1`); the squared amplitude of a coloured sector, `r² = N(1 − ω) = 3`, so `Q = 1/3 + r²/6 = 5/6`.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.koide_five_sixths
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2 — the up-quark Koide value: `Q = 5/6 ⟺ ρ² = 3/4`, that is `6 Σ a_j² = 5 â₀²` exactly when `4 â₁ â₂ = 3 â₀²` (beside `koide_two_thirds`, `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 â₁ â₂ = â₀²`); with `â₁ â₂ = N(b)` and `r² = 4N(b)/a²` this is `r² = 3`, the colour norm.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.koide_up_band
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2 — the up-quark Koide value in three schemes (`FlavourML.koide_up_band`).

C5.name: FRC.Flavour.trace_double
C5.doc: 28:C5, 00:G17 — the trace of the square of a unit: for `z z̄ = 1`, `z² + z̄² = (z + z̄)² − 2`; with `z = e^{iθ}` this is `2cos 2θ = (2cos θ)² − 2`. The lock `δ_d = δ₀/2` of 28:C5 is this relation between the cube invariants `c = cos 3δ` of the lepton and down sectors: `c_ℓ = 2 c_d² − 1`.

C5.name: FRC.Flavour.trace_triple
C5.doc: 28:C5, 00:G17 — the trace of the cube of a unit: for `z z̄ = 1`, `z³ + z̄³ = (z + z̄)³ − 3(z + z̄)`; with `z = e^{iθ}`, `2cos 3θ = (2cos θ)³ − 3(2cos θ)`. The lock `δ_u = δ₀/3` of 28:C5 is `c_ℓ = 4 c_u³ − 3 c_u` between the lepton and up cube invariants.

C5.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_det
C5.doc: 28:C1, 28:C5, 28:Z1 — the determinant of a circulant: `det (circ a b c) = a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc`; at `c = b̄` this is the cube invariant `∏ √m_k = a³ + 2 Re(b³) − 3a N(b)`, whose phase part `Re(b³)` carries the winding residue (28:Z1).

C6.name: FRC.Flavour.gst_relation
C6.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the Gatto–Sartori–Tonin relation. A symmetric two-by-two texture `R D Rᵀ` with `R` the rotation `(c, −s; s, c)`, `c² + s² = 1`, and `D = diag(m₁, m₂)` has the `(1,1)` entry `m₁ c² + m₂ s²`; when that entry vanishes (the texture zero), `m₂ s² = −m₁ c²`, that is `tan²θ = −m₁/m₂`: the Cabibbo angle from the two light masses.

C6.name: FRC.Flavour.cabibbo_modulus
C6.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the full Cabibbo relation: for a unit `z` (`z z̄ = 1`, the relative winding phase `e^{iφ}`) the modulus `|s_d c_u − c_d s_u z|² = s_d² c_u² + c_d² s_u² − s_d c_u c_d s_u T(z)` with `T(z) = z + z̄ = 2 cos φ`; with `s_d = √(m_d/m_s)` and `s_u = √(m_u/m_c)` this is `V_us = |√(m_d/m_s) − e^{iφ} √(m_u/m_c)|`.

C6.name: FRC.Flavour.gatto_leading
C6.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the Gatto relation's leading term and its value at φ = π/2 (`FlavourML.gatto_leading`).

C7.name: FRC.Flavour.texture_exponents

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_mul
C11.doc: 28:C11 — circulants are closed under the product: `circ a b c · circ a' b' c' = circ (aa' + bc' + cb') (ab' + ba' + cc') (ac' + bb' + ca')`.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_adj
C11.doc: 28:C11 — the adjugate of a circulant is a circulant: `adj (circ a b c) = circ (a² − bc) (c² − ab) (b² − ac)`.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.seesaw_circulant
C11.doc: 28:C11, 28:X11, 00:G15 — the seesaw of circulants is circulant: `m_D · adj(M_R) · m_Dᵀ` is a circulant whenever `m_D` and `M_R` are (the inverse `M_R⁻¹ = adj(M_R)/det M_R` differs from the adjugate by the scalar), so the light neutrinos are Koide-form.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.transpose_fixed_point
C11.doc: 28:C11, 28:X11, 28:P5, 00:G15 — the transpose fixed point. With `M_R = c · m_D` (the `126` alignment, 28:Y1) the seesaw collapses: `m_D · adj(c m_D) · m_Dᵀ = c² det(m_D) · m_Dᵀ`, a scalar multiple of the transpose, so the light neutrinos carry the Dirac eigenvalues (`circ_transpose`, `circ_eigen`: the transpose circulant has the eigenvalues `λ_{-k}`), the amplitude `r_ν = r_D` and the Koide value `Q_ν = Q_D = 2/3` of the colourless Dirac mass.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_transpose
C11.doc: 28:C11, 28:P5 — the transpose of a circulant is the circulant of the reversed row: `(circ a b c)ᵀ = circ a c b`.

C11b.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sumsq
C11b.doc: 28:C1, 28:C2, 28:C11b — the squares of the eigenvalues sum to `3a² + 6bc`: at `c = b̄` this is `3a² + 6 N(b)`, so `Q = Σλ²/(Σλ)² = 1/3 + (2/3) N(b)/a²`, the Koide form with `ρ² = N(b)/a²` (`koide_parseval`).

C12.name: FRC.Interactions.reflection_algebra
C12.doc: 00:G12, 28:C12 — the reflection algebra of four directions: the `16` basis elements `e_S`, `S ⊆ {0, 1, 2, 3}`, close under the product; the product is associative on the basis; distinct directions anticommute, `e_i e_j = −e_j e_i`, and each squares to zero.

C12.name: FRC.Interactions.fifth_direction
C12.doc: 00:G12, 27:C9, 28:C12 — the quarter-turn as the fifth direction maps the sixteen `e_S` of four directions one-to-one onto the sixteen even subsets of five directions, the chiral spinor `16`; for `|S|` odd the image is the product `e_S e_4` with sign `+1`.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_parseval
X1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C1, 28:X1 — Parseval on the cube-root orbit `C₃`: for amplitudes `a₀, a₁, a₂` and `ω` with `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`, `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 â₁ â₂`, `â₀ = Σ a_j`, `â₁ = a₀ + a₁ω + a₂ω²`, `â₂ = a₀ + a₁ω² + a₂ω` — the Koide form `Q = Σ a_j² / (Σ a_j)² = 1/3 + (2/3)ρ²` with `ρ² = â₁â₂/â₀²`, exact on every shell carrying the root `ω`.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_extension
X1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C2, 28:X1, 28:P1, on every shell: with `h + h = 1` and `ν = −3`, `ω = −h + h w` has `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`; `â₂ = â̄₁`, so `â₁ â₂ = N(â₁)`; Parseval `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 N(â₁)`; and `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 N(â₁) = â₀²` (`ρ² = 1/2`).

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_half
X1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:X1 — the hypotheses of `koide_extension` hold on every frame `p = 4κ + 1`, the Carrier included: `h = 2κ + 1` has `h + h = 1`, and `ν = −3` has `ν + 3 = 0`.

X2.name: FRC.Flavour.norm_one_sub_omega

X2.name: FRC.Flavour.koide_five_sixths

X4.name: FRC.Flavour.cabibbo_modulus
X4.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the full Cabibbo relation: for a unit `z` (`z z̄ = 1`, the relative winding phase `e^{iφ}`) the modulus `|s_d c_u − c_d s_u z|² = s_d² c_u² + c_d² s_u² − s_d c_u c_d s_u T(z)` with `T(z) = z + z̄ = 2 cos φ`; with `s_d = √(m_d/m_s)` and `s_u = √(m_u/m_c)` this is `V_us = |√(m_d/m_s) − e^{iφ} √(m_u/m_c)|`.

X7.name: FRC.Flavour.quarter_turn_boundary

X7.name: FRC.Flavour.lo_eigen

X7.name: FRC.Flavour.lo_ratio_sq
X7.doc: 28:C3, 28:X7 — with `s² = 3`, `(3 − s)² = (7 − 4s)(3 + s)²`: the leading-order ratio `(λ₂/λ₀)² = m_μ/m_τ` is `7 − 4√3 = (2 − √3)² ≈ 0.0718` (observed `0.0595`).
